description: UMH (Universal Mastery Hierarchy) 13-layer production stack design — UMH is an orchestration/governance platform, not a Trinity app frontend product
note: UMH is fundamentally different from EOS/CreatorOS/LyfeOS. It is the control plane, orchestrator, governance layer, and production truth authority. Its 13-layer stack reflects this role.

layers.desired_end_state: Cockpit web UI at universalmetaharness.tech. Operator dashboard for governance, approvals, monitoring, work packet management, organism status. React/TypeScript on Fly.io.
layers.current_state: Cockpit deployed to Fly.io at universalmetaharness.tech. WorldView design system. Panels for organism, governance, execution, runtime status. Production-deployed and functional.
layers.gap: Cockpit exists and is deployed. Ongoing enhancement needed for new governance features (work packets, 13-layer readiness, Socratic question UI). Not a Trinity app frontend gap — cockpit is operational.
layers.implementation_status: OPERATIONAL — cockpit is live. Enhancement deferred to future phases.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: UMH cockpit is separate from Trinity apps. React/TypeScript shared. Design system is UMH-specific (WorldView).
layers.app_specific_notes: UMH cockpit is an operator tool, not a consumer product. Different UX standards apply. Operator experience is the priority, not consumer aesthetics.
validation_requirements: Operator can see status and approve actions

layers.desired_end_state: UMH substrate API. Organism/governance/execution/settings routes. Python bridges for CLI integration. SignalEnvelope processing. Work packet management API. Production truth API.
layers.current_state: UMH API routes deployed in transports/api/http/. Python bridges in transports/api/. Substrate gateway operational. Organism, governance, system, execution, settings routes functional.
layers.gap: API exists and is functional. New endpoints needed for Phase 14.5A governance features (Socratic questions, 13-layer readiness, contradiction/clarification ledgers). These are future enhancements, not current gaps.
layers.implementation_status: OPERATIONAL — core API is live. Enhancement deferred.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: UMH API is Python-based (substrate), not Express/TypeScript like Trinity apps.
layers.app_specific_notes: UMH API serves the operator experience, not end users. Different performance and scale requirements than Trinity app APIs.

layers.desired_end_state: Neon Postgres for platform state (users, orgs, portfolios). File-based data store for artifacts, proofs, audit docs. Runtime config store for dynamic configuration. Production truth archive.
layers.current_state: Neon Postgres operational for platform state. File-based artifact store at data/umh/. Runtime config store operational. Production truth promotion pipeline functional.
layers.gap: Database is operational. Schema may need expansion for new governance features. File storage is git-backed (artifacts committed to repo). No object storage for large files.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Neon Postgres shared. UMH uses Python/Drizzle (via TypeScript sidecar) and psycopg2 directly.
layers.app_specific_notes: UMH database stores orchestration state, not product data. Trinity app data stays in their own databases. UMH may store cross-app metadata (production truth status, governance decisions).

layers.desired_end_state: Operator authentication for cockpit access. API key authentication for programmatic access. Role-based access (operator, observer, automated agent). Future: Clerk for cockpit auth if multiple operators.
layers.current_state: Basic auth on cockpit. API auth for programmatic access. Single operator (founder). No multi-user auth required yet.
layers.gap: Single-operator auth is functional. Multi-operator auth not needed until team grows. Clerk integration for cockpit is future state, not current need.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: UMH auth is independent from Trinity app auth. Different requirements (operator vs consumer).
layers.app_specific_notes: UMH is single-operator currently. Auth complexity is low. When multiple operators are needed, Clerk or similar can be added.

layers.desired_end_state: Cockpit on Fly.io. Substrate services on VPS via Docker. Discord bot on VPS. Operator API on VPS. Distributed execution across VPS + Beast.
layers.current_state: Cockpit deployed to Fly.io. Docker containers on VPS (os-discord, os-operator, os-webhook, os-scraper). VPS is the orchestration hub.
layers.gap: Deployment is operational. Docker containers run on VPS. Cockpit on Fly.io. Some containers may need resource optimization (VPS is resource-constrained).
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Fly.io for cockpit. Docker for VPS services. Different from Trinity app deployment (which is all Fly.io).
layers.app_specific_notes: UMH has a hybrid deployment: Fly.io for web UI, VPS Docker for services, Beast for heavy compute. This is by design — VPS is the coordination brain.

layers.desired_end_state: VPS = lightweight orchestrator/control plane (always-on). Beast = GPU workhorse for heavy compute, model inference, media processing. Fly.io = cockpit hosting. Neon = managed database.
layers.current_state: VPS operational as orchestrator. Beast available for heavy compute via SSH/Tailscale. Fly.io hosting cockpit. Neon providing database.
layers.gap: Compute architecture is operational. VPS has resource constraints (Hostinger, 90% steal reported). Beast is available but not always-on. Compute balance is functional but not optimized.
layers.implementation_status: OPERATIONAL — compute is functional with known constraints.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: UMH compute architecture is unique — hybrid VPS/Beast/Fly.io. Trinity apps use Fly.io only.
layers.app_specific_notes: VPS steal time is a known issue. Beast compensates for heavy work. This is an active architecture, not a gap to close.

layers.desired_end_state: GitHub as version control (antonyfmunoz/OS). Direct commit to main (solo founder phase). Feature branches for experimental/risky changes. Pre-commit hooks for type coherence, instance leak, projection leak, dependency direction. Automated cockpit deploy to Fly.io.
layers.current_state: GitHub repo operational. Direct commit to main. Pre-commit hooks installed (4 gates). Manual cockpit deploy via flyctl. No automated CI/CD pipeline.
layers.gap: No automated CI/CD pipeline. Pre-commit hooks provide local gating but no CI validation. Cockpit deployment is manual.
layers.implementation_status: OPERATIONAL — version control and hooks work. CI/CD automation is enhancement.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: GitHub shared. Pre-commit hooks are UMH-specific. CI/CD automation would be UMH-specific.
layers.app_specific_notes: Solo founder phase means direct commit to main is acceptable. CI/CD becomes important when team grows or when deployment frequency increases.

layers.desired_end_state: RLS on platform tables (users, orgs). Pre-commit security gates (no secrets, no instance leaks, no projection leaks). Governance engine for execution risk classification. Audit trail for all governance decisions.
layers.current_state: Pre-commit hooks enforce 4 security gates. Governance engine classifies execution risk. No RLS on platform tables. Audit trail exists in artifact files.
layers.gap: No RLS on Neon platform tables. Pre-commit hooks provide code-level security. Governance engine provides execution-level security. Database-level security (RLS) is the gap.
layers.implementation_status: PARTIALLY OPERATIONAL — code and execution security exists. Database RLS is missing.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: RLS principles shared with Trinity apps. Pre-commit gates are UMH-specific.
layers.app_specific_notes: UMH security is multi-layered: code gates (pre-commit), execution gates (governance engine), and should include database gates (RLS). The first two are strong. The third is missing.

layers.desired_end_state: Rate limiting on cockpit API. Rate limiting on public-facing endpoints. AI call rate limiting (cost control).
layers.current_state: No explicit rate limiting. AI calls have cost controls via model router (economy mode, fallback chain). Cockpit API not rate-limited.
layers.gap: No HTTP-level rate limiting. AI cost control exists via model router but is not rate limiting per se.
layers.implementation_status: NOT IMPLEMENTED — low priority for single-operator system.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Rate limiting principles shared but UMH has different threat model (single operator vs public users).
layers.app_specific_notes: UMH is not public-facing (except cockpit). Single-operator system has low rate limiting urgency. AI cost control is more important than HTTP rate limiting.

layers.desired_end_state: CDN for cockpit static assets (Fly.io built-in). In-memory caching for hot substrate state. Graph query caching.
layers.current_state: Fly.io provides basic CDN for cockpit. No explicit API caching. Graph queries run fresh each time.
layers.gap: Basic CDN exists via Fly.io. No API or substrate caching. Graph query caching would improve performance.
layers.implementation_status: PARTIALLY OPERATIONAL — CDN exists. Caching is enhancement.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: CDN via Fly.io shared pattern. Substrate caching is UMH-specific.
layers.app_specific_notes: Performance optimization. Not a production blocker.

layers.desired_end_state: Fly.io scaling for cockpit. VPS Docker resource limits for services. Beast handles overflow compute. No single point of failure for critical paths.
layers.current_state: Single Fly.io machine for cockpit. VPS Docker containers without resource limits. Beast available for overflow.
layers.gap: No Docker resource limits on VPS containers. No Fly.io scaling configured. VPS is a single point of failure.
layers.implementation_status: PARTIALLY OPERATIONAL — works at current scale. Not production-hardened for growth.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Fly.io scaling shared. Docker resource management is UMH-specific.
layers.app_specific_notes: VPS has resource constraints. Docker containers should have resource limits to prevent runaway processes from taking down the VPS. This is a production hardening item.

layers.desired_end_state: Centralized error recording (substrate/observability/error_recorder.py). Docker container logs. Cockpit status panels. Discord notification for critical errors. Structured logging across all services.
layers.current_state: Error recorder exists in substrate. Docker logs available via docker logs. Cockpit has status panels. Discord notifications functional. Logging is mixed (structured in some places, console in others).
layers.gap: Error recording exists but logging is inconsistent. No external error tracking service. No log aggregation. Discord notifications are the primary alerting mechanism.
layers.implementation_status: PARTIALLY OPERATIONAL — error recording and Discord alerts work. Logging consistency and aggregation are gaps.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: PostHog for analytics (if desired). Error tracking approach shared question with Trinity apps.
layers.app_specific_notes: UMH error recording is substrate-native. External services (Sentry, PostHog) are optional enhancements. Discord notifications serve as the primary alert channel for the founder.
validation_requirements: Discord alerts fire on critical errors

layers.desired_end_state: VPS auto-restart for Docker containers. Neon automatic backups. Cockpit Fly.io redundancy. Git-backed artifact recovery. Production truth promotion as recovery checkpoint.
layers.current_state: Docker containers restart on failure (restart: unless-stopped). Neon has automatic backups. Fly.io has release rollback. Git provides artifact version history. Production truth promotion creates recovery checkpoints.
layers.gap: Recovery strategy is implicit, not documented. No formal runbook. No disaster recovery test. Production truth promotion is the strongest recovery mechanism (known-good state can be restored).
layers.implementation_status: PARTIALLY OPERATIONAL — restart and backup mechanisms exist. Formal recovery documentation and testing are missing.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Recovery principles shared. Production truth promotion is UMH-specific.
layers.app_specific_notes: UMH production truth promotion is a unique recovery advantage — every promoted phase is a known-good checkpoint. Recovery = roll back to last promoted truth.

summary.note: UMH is fundamentally different from Trinity apps. Most layers are already operational because UMH is a live production system. Gaps are hardening, not greenfield.
